title: The date
hook: Anas carries a newborn and a handful of dates across Medina

segments.voice: Yesterday, the call in the ear, and your line: the first words. Did one of your first words to someone today land as a welcome? After the first sound comes the first taste. Day one thousand three hundred nineteen.

Umm Sulaym has just given birth, and her son Anas is carrying the newborn through Medina to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. She has sent some dates along with him. Anas tells the story in Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase. The Prophet takes the baby and asks: is there anything with him? Yes, some dates. He takes one, chews it until it's soft, and puts a little of it into the baby's mouth. Today's word is that small act: tahnik.
screen: `ANAS CARRIES A NEWBORN.` → `IS THERE ANYTHING WITH HIM?` → `A SOFTENED DATE FOR THE BABY.`

segments.voice: First, the scene, finished. In Bukhari, the Prophet then named the baby 'Abdullah. Sahih Muslim keeps a fuller version of Anas's telling, in paraphrase: the baby moved his tongue and licked at the date, and the Prophet said, see the Ansar's love of dates. The Ansar were the people of Medina, and dates were their harvest. A joke, a taste and a name, all in one visit. Second, it happens again. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari tells, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: a son was born to me, and I took him to the Prophet. He named him Ibrahim, did tahnik for him with a date, prayed for blessing for him, and gave him back to me. So tahnik isn't a single moment in one family. The Prophet did it more than once, when newborns were brought to him. Third, what tahnik is. A date is softened, by chewing or by mashing, and a little is touched to the inside of the baby's mouth, at the palate. In Abu Musa's report it comes with a du'a for blessing. Some Muslim families still keep the custom, and some ask a respected, pious person to do it. Fourth, why a date? The texts don't explain it, and it's honest to say so. They only show it: in the moment of welcome, the Prophet reached for something sweet. Before the baby could know a single word, he gave it a taste, and a prayer. Whatever the child meets later in life, the first thing put to its mouth was sweet, offered with kindness, by someone who prayed for it.
screen: `SEE HOW THE ANSAR LOVE DATES.` · `ABU MUSA: IBRAHIM, A DATE, A DU'A.` · `A SOFTENED DATE TO THE PALATE.` · `THE TEXTS SHOW IT; THEY DON'T EXPLAIN.`

segments.voice: The practice: eat a date thankfully. If you have a date, or anything sweet nearby, hold it. If not, picture one. Settle, and breathe. Look at it before you eat it. Then take one slow bite. Let it sit on your tongue, the way it would for someone tasting sweetness for the first time. Don't rush to swallow. If you pray, you can say bismillah before, and alhamdulillah after. If not, simply notice the sweetness, and who might have made it reach you. The bell holds the time.
Tahnik. Touching a softened date to a newborn's palate, with a prayer for blessing, as the Prophet did for babies brought to him. Today's word.

Your line: sweetness first. Today, when you meet someone new, or someone small, let the first thing you offer be something sweet: a kind word, a treat, a smile. Tomorrow, the naming. Day one thousand three hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Muslim families who keep the custom perform tahnik soon after birth: a softened date is touched to the inside of the baby's mouth, sometimes by a respected or pious person, with a du'a for blessing.

fork.setup: Anas arrives with Umm Sulaym's newborn and a handful of dates. what does the Prophet do?
options: hands the dates back to Anas to eat.
chews a date soft and puts a little in the baby's mouth.
blesses the dates and sends them home with Anas.
fork.reveal: he softened a date and gave the baby a taste, then named him 'Abdullah (Bukhari). in Muslim's version he adds: see the Ansar's love of dates.

original.note: Arabic: tahnik, touching a softened date to a newborn's palate.

trapdoor: what you thought: a sweet treat for a baby.
what it means: tahnik: a softened date touched to the newborn's palate, with a name and a prayer for blessing.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 5467 (Abu Musa) and 5470 (Anas): in both reports the Prophet's tahnik came with a name, and in Abu Musa's with a du'a for blessing.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5470 (Anas: Umm Sulaym's son; 'is there anything with him?'; the chewed date; named 'Abdullah)
Sahih Muslim 2144 (Anas's fuller version: the baby licks the date; 'the Ansar's love of dates')
Sahih al-Bukhari 5467 (Abu Musa: his son named Ibrahim, given tahnik with a date, blessing prayed for)

notes: Hadith numbers to confirm: Bukhari 5467, 5470. In 5470 the baby is the son of Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym; Anas is Umm Sulaym's son. Confirm details (Umm Sulaym sending the baby; the Prophet's remark about the Ansar).
Teach says 'Muslim families still keep the custom, and some ask a respected, pious person': this is a general claim not in the cited text. Keeper to confirm or soften.
Trapdoor limits the du'a-and-name claim to the two cited reports.
Sensitivity: the Bukhari 5470 narration is preceded by the death of an earlier child of Abu Talhah; not mentioned here.

Editor: attribution fix: the baby licking the date and the 'Ansar's love of dates' remark are in Sahih Muslim 2144, not Bukhari 5470; teach, fork reveal and sources now say so. Cut 'a boy named Anas' (an unsourced age claim) and the hook's 'the baby begins to work his tongue' from the Bukhari scene; removed 'then laughed' (not in the text); du'a now attributed only to Abu Musa's report; 'Muslim families still keep the custom' softened to 'some Muslim families'. Confirm Muslim 2144 numbering and wording.
